title: Check and shrink
prompt:
Implement two functions of a mini property engine:

- `check_roundtrip_codec(encode, decode, samples)` — for each sample, `decode(encode(x))` must equal `x` (any exception counts as failure). Returns `(passed, first_failure)` — the failing sample or `None`.
- `shrink(samples, bad)` — minimize a failing list: repeatedly try removing one element and keep the removal when the property (identity round-trip via `check_roundtrip_codec`) still fails; stop when no single removal keeps it failing or one element remains. Returns the minimal list.

Shrinking is what turns 'fails on this 50-element monster' into 'fails on `["\x00"]`' — the bug report the author can act on.

tests.name: clean codec passes, broken codec fails
tests.code:
ok, fail = check_roundtrip_codec(lambda x: x.upper(), lambda x: x.lower(), ['ab', 'Cd'])
assert ok is False and fail == 'Cd'   # lower(upper('Cd')) == 'cd' != 'Cd'
ok, fail = check_roundtrip_codec(lambda x: x, lambda x: x, ['ab', 'Cd'])
assert ok is True and fail is None
print('ok')
tests.hint: The property catches what an example test never imagined.

tests.name: shrinking finds the minimal failing list
tests.code:
def bad_encode(items):
    return [x for x in items if x != 7]  # drops 7s: round-trip fails on any list containing one
bad = [1, 2, 7, 3]
minimal = shrink(bad, bad)
assert minimal == [7] or (7 in minimal and len(minimal) == 1), minimal
print('ok')
tests.hint: Remove elements while the property still fails; one 7 remains.
